chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Abu Jameela from Ismail ibn Abu Idris from Al-Husayn ibn Zamara ibn Abu Zamara from his father from his grandfather who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'The rulings of the Muslims are upon three – Just testimony, or a conclusive oath, or a past Sunnah of the Imams (peace be upon him) of the Guidance'.
ai.seo_question: What are the three primary sources of legal rulings for Muslims according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delineates the tripartite sources of legal authority for the Muslim community: just testimony, a conclusive oath, and the established Sunnah of the Imams of Guidance. This classification underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the Imams' living tradition as a primary source of law alongside evidentiary proofs, reflecting the continuity of divine guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt.
